title: Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes
coverage: This was a partial audit of a 9,500-line paper, with these parts read closely and checked line by line. Sec 1 (statement). All of Sec 2: directed colimits, small-code recovery, the uniform Hanf-type reduction, the Erdos-Rado-style partition lemma and the EM order presentation. All of Sec 3: the H(delta) order facts, balance of cuts (checked case by case), segments near small cuts, the short-sequence orbit theorem, the orbit/record bound, ordinal support closure, appending an indecomposable segment, alignment, and the elimination argument for reversal, including the profile pigeonhole, the a^theta <= mu and tau_mu > a bookkeeping, and the persistence step. All of Sec 4: stabilization of strong-map classes, back-and-forth categoricity at countable-cofinality closure points, parameter-orbit counting (which relies on well-orders having few cuts), the block-transposition tree argument, the ordinal-vector lemma, uniform testing, compact placement (event counting), unique lifts, and amalgamation with the singleton-type bound. Sec 6: approximation sequences, stationary free extension, average descent, products and symmetry (the kappa/lambda = kappa^+ array argument), and local character. All of Sec 10: nonalgebraicity of free lifts, the minimal-type splitting-tree count, the containment test, the pregeometry axioms, base change, anchored prescriptions, the no-growth theorem (directed system of J_n, distinct marks, colimit of size mu with at most lambda points, against pointed categoricity), and tail no-growth. Sec 9: finite marked systems and projection all-domination, the joint boundary diagram return-tree argument, completion, the fixed-parameter boundary lemma, and exact boundary lifting. Sec 11: shapes, relative bases and structural lemmas. The Sec 12 main exact-lifting proof and the internal realization lemma. Sec 13: uniform definitions, the bound register, the G_j hierarchy and absorption, and common levels. All of Sec 14: subcube selection and the cardinal induction in the successor, regular-limit and singular cases, with the added-axis trick, pointed categoricity and the final tail theorem. Only skimmed or not read: Sec 5 (working schemes and the diagram clause), Sec 7 (relative isolation, primeness, all-lengths existence), Sec 8 (marked-pair template, two-part testing, chain closure, the marked package), Sec 11 (tiled presentations, conditional package, classification with basis maps) and the rest of Sec 12 (joint boundary comparisons, tiled testing). Many sampled steps rely on these sections as black boxes, for example the primeness of all-dominated increments and the saturation and homogeneity clauses of the working package.
main_claim: For every infinite lambda there is a mu(lambda) such that any AEC with LS(K) <= lambda that is categorical in some kappa >= mu(lambda) is categorical in every kappa' >= mu(lambda). This is Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in ZFC, with no amalgamation, tameness or large-cardinal hypotheses. Through a set-coding reduction it is equivalent to the claim that categoricity in unboundedly many cardinals implies categoricity on a tail.
